title: 'He was loved': Family holds vigil for man killed by police on Memorial Drive
subtitle: 'We're gathered here today in his memory to celebrate his life and also to put some humanity into the whole event'
article: Family of a man shot dead by police during a chase on a busy Calgary roadway last year gathered Wednesday to commemorate the one-year anniversary of his death, remembering him as a loving and kind father, grandfather and son.

Levon Fox was one of two men killed on May 29, 2023, when police opened fire on a stolen cube van that had led officers on a slow-speed chase down Memorial Drive, the other being the driver of the vehicle, Wesley Davidson. Dennis Wildman, Fox's brother, was also a passenger in the vehicle; he was taken to hospital in police custody after the incident.

On Wednesday, Fox's family held a vigil close to the spot where he died at the intersection of Memorial Drive and Edmonton Trail. Fox was 39 years old when he died, a father of four and a new grandfather.

Family members and other loved ones, many from Stoney Nakoda First Nation, sang songs, beat drums, prayed and tossed flowers into the Bow River in Fox's memory.

"We're gathered here today in his memory to celebrate his life and also to put some humanity into the whole event," said Lena Wildman, the mother to the brothers. "People need to take a step back and remember that these are people. He wasn't an unwanted person; he was loved."
Wildman said Fox was an incredibly kind and giving person who had a deep love for his family.
"He was always looking out for others," she said.

Both of her sons have struggled with addiction, Wildman said, but in the months leading up to his death, Fox "worked so hard to break away from that life" and support his family. He was waiting to go into treatment at the time of his death.
Fox was in Calgary to "rescue" his older brother, said Wildman, and the two were looking for a ride home to Morley.
"They were passengers in that vehicle," said Wildman. "The driver offered them a ride and they were thinking, 'That's my ride home.' "
Fox's brother has been in addiction treatment and recovery programs in the year since the incident but is still reeling from the trauma it caused, said Wildman.
Sitting on a bench along the banks of the Bow River, Wildman motioned toward the nearby Calgary Drop-In Centre and said, "I know there's a lot of our people over there struggling.

"The message I want to put out there to families is never give up on them," she said. "I never give up on my kids, knowing they're battling addiction. I always say prayers. I always ask creator to bring them peace."

Tara McHugh, the mother of one of Fox's adult daughters, said addiction had stripped her daughter of a close bond with her father for much of her life. She said Fox had started to turn a corner before his death and was becoming more involved in his daughter's life, making his loss even tougher.
"It's been a struggle, but she's doing the best that she can," said McHugh. "Today, though, it just brings back a lot of emotions."
McHugh said she's seen videos of the incident shared on social media and maintains that the police response that day was excessive.
"There was no need for guns," McHugh said. "There were other methods that could have been used to stop the truck that day."

Said Wildman: "The force of police, it's really too much. Instead of asking them to show their hands, identify yourselves, what do they do? They shoot at them, and unfortunately two people died. That was so unnecessary, and it really bothers me."

At the time of the incident, police said a security guard at a private property in Mayland Heights reported three suspicious men who'd fled in a stolen cube van. Police said it was driven erratically as it left the neighbourhood - hitting a barricade and a building - and multiple officers began tailing the vehicle as it travelled down Memorial Drive.

Officers attempted to pull over the vehicle and confine it multiple times, according to police, but due to "rapidly changing dynamics," an officer discharged their firearm. Witnesses told Postmedia that day that they saw police shoot through the driver and passenger windows of the van.
Alberta's police watchdog, the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team, said Wednesday its investigation into the matter is ongoing.
